title: Calculation Note: Funding-Month Interest on a Closing and Funding Loan
content:
**Formal clause.** Funding-month interest is the prepaid interest a borrower pays after closing for the month in which a Closing and Funding loan funded, where the disbursement date falls after the last day of the charge collected at closing. For funding-month interest, the charge collected at closing is the closing's prepaid interest charge booked on the signing date.

1. **Days.** The funding-month interest runs from the disbursement date through the last day of the disbursement month, both days counted; the disbursement month's last day is the day before the first day of the following month, February having 29 days in a year divisible by four and 28 otherwise, April, June, September and November 30 and every other month 31; it is found as the days from the disbursement date to the first payment date, which falls on the first day of the second month after the disbursement month, less the days of the month in between.
2. **Daily amount of every other entry.** A prepaid interest entry other than a funding-month interest payment or a per diem shortfall payment, the charge collected at closing included, keeps the per diem policy's daily amount: the closing's loan amount times its note rate taken as a percent, divided by the per diem day-count basis, rounded to the per diem rounding decimals.
3. **Funding-month per diem.** For funding-month interest, and never for a per diem shortfall, the per diem is the loan file's loan amount times the rate the closing's lock holds, taken as a percent, divided by the per diem day-count basis of the closing method, rounded half up to the cent.
4. **Interest.** The funding-month interest is its days times that per diem, rounded half up to the cent.
5. **Redraw fee refunds.** The redraw fee refunds on the closing, the reversals of doc redraw fee charges for the part charged above Larkspur's redraw schedule (reversals marked as the part not in the fee schedule on the closing's fee ledger), are applied to the funding-month interest the borrower owes rather than paid out separately.
6. **Amount paid.** The amount the borrower pays is the funding-month interest less the setoff and less the redraw fee refunds, rounded half up to the cent and never below zero, plus any payment channel charge. The standard funding-month payment carries no setoff and no payment channel charge.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| charge collected at closing | 28 January through 31 January |
| disbursement date | 3 February 2026 (after the charge's last day) |
| first payment date | 1 April 2026 |
| loan file's loan amount; rate the lock holds; day-count basis | 400,000.00; 6.5 percent; 365 |
| redraw fee refunds on the closing | one reversal of 40.00 |

- Days: 3 February to 1 April is 57 days; less the 31 days of March, the month in between, gives 26 (3 February through 28 February, both counted).
- Per diem: 400,000.00 times 6.5 percent, divided by 365, is 71.2329, rounded to 71.23.
- Interest: 26 times 71.23 is 1,851.98.
- Less the 40.00 redraw fee refund: 1,811.98, which the borrower pays.

In a year divisible by four, a loan disbursed on 10 February with a first payment date of 1 April counts 51 days less 31, which is 20 days (10 through 29 February). Had the disbursement date been 30 January, within the charge, the condition for funding-month interest would not be met.
